purpose: ONE timing decision for an OFP station notice. The app (dashboard chart, PDF map marks, NOTAM records) and ODSS (airport cards, PDF consequences, PDF cards) each read the same LIDO record from the same OFP; both evaluate it with these rules, byte-identical in both repos (app notam-timing-rules.json = ODSS app/odss/notam_timing_rules.json), and both suites run tests/fixtures/notam-timing-vectors.json. Item 3 (Gatwick, 14 Oct 2026): the decision was made by three evaluators with three rule sets.

stationWindows.readFrom: Operator default: NOTAM validity is assessed two hours either side of the station time (app 94a7019, 25 Jul 2026; HelpYou plan A8, 30 Jul 2026: 'window default +/-2h stays'). ODSS had kept a one-hour departure window, so a closure 60-120 min from ETD was drawn on the chart and the PDF map but absent from the card and the PDF text.

noReferenceStations.note: Destination alternates, EDTO, fuel-enroute and enroute stations: the app holds no reference instant (window ETA-2h to ETA+24h, boss 02 Sep chart ruling); ODSS judges alternates at the destination ETA (ETA +/-2h), EDTO at sector entry, fuel-enroute and enroute at departure. That policy is the product owner's to choose; until then each runtime keeps its own window and reference for those roles. The evaluation rules below are shared for every role.

rules: The LIDO VALID range is start ' - ' end. No start, or no end that reads as a date-time, UFN or PERM, is a timing review: an absent end is never read as open-ended.
UFN and PERM are open-ended: in force from the start, no end is invented.
An EST end is held as the end (flagged estimated), as both runtimes did before this spec.
Start is inclusive and end is exclusive.

syntax.note: The syntactic text (I5). A quote of any kind is removed when it wraps; a quote glued to letters or digits on both sides stays (O'CLOCK, 26'15, 15.0000"N); an opening quote (after a space, the start, a removed character, an opening bracket or an opening quote, before a non-space) pairs with the next closing quote of its kind (quotePairs; nested pairs close innermost first) and both are removed; a quote right after a digit that closes no opening quote stays as its unit mark (3000' - feet; '"3000'"' reads 3000'); any other quote is removed. A bracket, parenthesis or brace is removed when it wraps: an opener with a space (or nothing, or a removed character) before it, and the closer that matches it; a pair inside a token - its opener glued to the token (OCA(OCH), 600(L/R), 40103(B)(3)) or its closer glued to what follows ((A)2020) - stays, and a closer with no opener stays only after one to three letters or digits that open their token (labelCloser: F), 1), IV)). An ellipsis (two or more stops) is removed. A colon is removed unless a digit is on each side (08:00). A dash with a space on either side joins nothing and is removed unless the tokens on both sides are range sides (rangeSide: a token holding a digit, a weekday, a month, a period word, UFN, PERM or a clock's designator: '1800 - 2000', 'MON - FRI', '27NOV25 - UFN', '2359 UTC - UFN' keep it; 'UNTIL - 121.35' loses it); at a line's edge a dash is kept when the token on its one side is a range side (a range wrapped over two lines: 'AUG 16 1800-' / '2000'), and a dash alone on its line is kept; the field's lines and the free text's lines are then each joined into one stream and read again, so punctuation across a line break reads as within a line ('UNTIL' / '-' / '121.35' reads 'UNTIL 121.35'). A removed quote or bracket leaves a space only where it alone kept two letters or digits apart ('(1)APPLY'), a removed colon or dash leaves a space; spaces are collapsed and a space before a boundary (boundaryPunctuation: ',', ';', a sentence period) is dropped. Removing, inserting or moving any of these characters around a token never changes the syntactic text, so it never changes a masking decision or a reading. A clause ends at clauseBoundary - a semicolon, or a period followed by a space or the end; a period inside a number, a domain or an abbreviation glued to the next word never ends one - and every relation that reads a sentence (contactHours, temporalObject) reads it by that one boundary.

A telephone number after TEL/PHONE/FAX/FOR INFO, or written with a leading + (+65 6123 4567). G4: up to six groups, single digits included ('+33 1 48 62 43 92').

A telephone number in a fixed national format, whole (with an AT before it): 617-561-1919, (866) 598-9522, 07484 424457, 03-3268-3111, 02 6128 4339, 0411 253 135. QA518: '866 598-9522' (the area code's brackets are punctuation).

A number (or a number range or list of sectors) with its unit: 1800-2000FT AMSL, 2400 M, 210 KNOTS, 3 DEG, 180-DEGREE, 15.00 DME, 841 MSL, 1 700 M (thousands spaced), 190-205 DEG. G2: a unit after a bracketed or signed number ('(-0.5)NM'), a fraction before INCH ('1/10TH INCH'), dimensions sharing a unit ('90 X 90 CM'); a stop that is not a decimal point is punctuation ('APPROACH...473 FT').
A number of seconds, or a range of them, with the unit: 300 SEC (an interval) - never holding a clock-like range.
A number of minutes, or a range of them, with the unit: 30 MIN, 15 AND 30 MINUTES (minutes are intervals, never periods).
A flight level or a flight-level band: FL110, FL 245-460, 470FL/660FL.
A route or sector altitude (MOCA, MSA, MEA, MORA ...), its segment or up to three named points first - never a weekday, month or period word: 'MOCA FROM CUTOX TO CUJKE 1200 TO 1900'.

rules: Item D is printed as the first body line(s) of a LIDO record. Typographic hyphens and dashes (dashes) are read as '-'. The field is the leading run of body lines made only of schedule tokens (fieldLine), joined with one space: a D field wrapped over several lines is one field, wherever the line breaks ('AUG 16' then '1800-2000', 'AUG' then '16 1800-2000', 'AUG 16 1800-' then '2000').

The field is accepted only when the grammar below reads all of it. A leading run it cannot read in full - a date with no time, a clock written HH:MM (colonClock), '/' between two times, 2400, a zero-length range, an impossible date - is a timing review, never 'no schedule'.
Daylight, exception and holiday rules (reviewLanguage) are a timing review.

TEMPORAL CONTENT in the free text after the field is found by SHAPE, never by validity (temporal, every class named): any clock-LIKE shape whatever its values - 3 or 4 digits alone or with suffix letters (2500, 0860, 0800A, 0800GMT, 1800Z), 1 or 2 digits with a dot, colon, space or H and 2 more (08.00, 8:00, 08:00:00, 18 00, 18H00), 1 or 2 digits with an H (18H), a letter for a digit (080O, O800, 1O00; a lower-case l in a run holding a digit is first written I (letterForDigit), while an upper-case route designator such as L888 stays a designator; each line is first stripped of format characters and NFKC-normalised (normalisation), so a full-width or styled digit is a digit and no zero-width character splits a clock), 6 PM, 6 P.M., SIX O'CLOCK, and any of these, or a 2-digit number, on either side of a range connector (-, /, TO, TIL, TILL, UNTIL, THRU, THROUGH, AND: 0860-1060, 18-20, 0800-10, FROM 8 TO 10); a date-time group (6, 8 or 10 digits); any date or month form (01/09/2026, 01-09-26 ...); any weekday or day word (DAILY, DLY, WEEKDAYS, WEEKENDS, HOL, HOLIDAYS, DAYS, WEEK, MONTH ...); any period or daylight word (H24, HJ, HN, HX, HO, SR, SS, SUNRISE, SUNSET, DAYLIGHT, DARKNESS, NIGHT, NGT, EVENING, MORNING, AFTERNOON, DAWN, DUSK, MIDNIGHT, SUMMER, WINTER, SEASON, 24 HR); a reference to hours (HR, HOURS); a duration of an hour or longer (2 HR, 3 DAYS, SIX MONTHS - minutes are intervals, not periods); a UTC offset, or a time zone after a clock; an ordinal day (FIRST MONDAY, EVERY OTHER DAY); an activation reference (AUP, UUP, WHEN ACTIVATED). The grammar reads a clock only in its own forms (HHMM, HHMM with UTC or Z, a valid HHMM-HHMM range); any other clock-like shape leaves its statement unreadable: a review. Before that, spans POSITIVELY classified as not temporal, each by a stated non-temporal context (benign: each class with its note - frequencies, telephone numbers, numbers with units, flight levels, route altitudes, altitudes and minima after their keyword, FAA take-off minima, declared distances, bearings, radials and sectors, designators, AIP pages, aircraft types and registrations, NOTAM and document numbers after their keyword, obstruction and permission case numbers, a document's own date, the verb MAY, the sun, marking and lighting by day or night, notice, permission and restoration lead times, contact-office hours, identifiers, positions, magnetic variation epochs, event years, observation times) are masked. A benign span never holds a clock-like range (benignNeverHolds) unless its class states allowClockRange, it never cuts a clock-like shape (benignNeverCuts: it may hold a whole one, as 'TORA 2100' does, never part of one), and it is never one side of a range: it is refused when a range connector joins it to temporal content left unmasked (rangeAbutment). A duration is benign ONLY in an explicit notice, permission or restoration context (PPR 48 HOURS, 24 HR PN, RE-OPN WI 2 HR, MAX RESTORATION TIME 04HRS, FPLS AT LEAST 3 HR BFR THE EOBT, NOTIFY ATC 24 HR IN ADVANCE); a duration attached to the restriction itself (CLSD FOR 2 HR, FOR MAX 2 HOURS, FOR A PERIOD OF 2 HOURS, DURING THE LAST 2 HOURS, WI 2 HR alone) is temporal content: a review, never a start.

Every temporal token must lie in a statement (statement): a maximal run of grammar vocabulary - clocks (with UTC or Z), day numbers, months, years, dates, weekdays, DLY, H24, UFN, PERM - joined by connectives (FROM, TO, UNTIL, THRU, THROUGH, UP TO, BTN/BETWEEN .. AND, ON, EVERY, EV, DURING, HR, THE HOURS OF, OPR HR, HR OF OPERATION, WITH EFFECT FROM, EFFECTIVE, UTC ...). A temporal token outside every statement is a review: there is no path from unmatched text to 'no schedule'. A statement is read whole or it is a review: after its trailing connectives are dropped, an exception, a negation or a local time (negations) makes it unreadable; dates are normalised (prepare: '27TH OF APR', 'AUGUST 16, 2026', ISO dates, BTN date AND date, 'CHANGED TO H24'); calendar periods with a year are read first (periodRange, periodSingle; a start preposition (startPrepositions) gives [date, open), an end preposition (endPrepositions) gives (open, date], ON or none a single day; a start with no time is the start of its day, an end with no time the end of its day; a start with no month or year takes the end's); the rest is rewritten into Item D syntax (rewrite) and read by the Item D grammar, days and hours bound together in either order ('SUN 1800-2000', '1800-2000 ON SUN', 'BTN 1700UTC TO 2200UTC EV SUN AND WED'). Bare numbers, UFN or PERM left alone (ignorable) read as nothing; any other leftover connective (fatal: a one-sided clock such as 'WEF 1800', 'AT 1800', 'UNTIL 1800') and any statement whose temporal content yields neither a period nor a schedule are a review. The free text reads as 'no schedule' only when it holds no temporal content of any shape.

Accounting. A statement holding periods only is accounted for when every period contains the whole B/C validity: a start (WEF, FROM, EFFECTIVE ...) at or before B, an end (UNTIL, TIL, TO ...) at or after C. A start after B - inside the validity or after C - or an end before C - inside it or before B - contradicts the validity and is a review (QA506-02); with an open end (UFN, PERM) an end date always narrows it. A statement holding a schedule must be proven equal, ON ITS OWN - never pooled with other statements, never by day parts or hours checked separately (QA506-03) - to the accepted Item D, or with no Item D to the whole validity (H24): by the same canonical rule set (each day part with its merged hours; all seven weekdays are daily), or by the same occurrences over the whole bounded validity (at most equivalenceEnumerationMaxDays days); a period in the statement clips its occurrences, and a clipped statement needs the bounded proof. An open-ended or longer validity with no structural equality is a review. With no readable validity, every temporal statement is a review. Hours alone ('BTN 0800-1000') are every day; days alone ('ACT MON-FRI') are those whole days.

QA514 (every digit accounted for). After the benign spans are masked, EVERY digit left (accountedResidue) is accounted for exactly as a temporal token is: it must lie in a statement the grammar reads whole and that is proven against Item D or B/C, else a review - there is no path to 'no schedule' while any digit is unaccounted for; the free text reads as 'no schedule' only when, masked, it holds no digit and no temporal content. Shape detection feeds the grammar; it is not the gate. A time in number words (FROM EIGHT TO TEN, TWO H) is temporal content (numberWordTime); a statement never starts right after a sign glued to its value (UNTIL +24 HR). Benign masks are governed by syntax (benignGovernance): a span that is the object of a temporal connective (DURING, OUTSIDE, UNTIL, TILL, TIL, FROM, BEFORE, AFTER, BTN/BETWEEN, AT, BY, WEF, TO, THRU, SINCE - TO, FROM and BY after an amendment verb or UP/SUBJECT take a value) and begins with a digit or a time word is never masked unless it is self-evidently not a time (a unit of length, height, speed, mass, angle or proportion - never a frequency, never minutes or seconds -, a flight level, a position, an approach-minimum pair, a CFR title, a DME distance, the sun as a light source): 'CLSD UNTIL 121.9' is a review; and DURING, DRG, OUTSIDE, SINCE and WEF only ever take a period, so whatever follows them and holds a digit is never masked unless self-evident ('CLSD DRG PHASE 2'). An office's hours (contactHours) are benign only when a contact verb governs them - the nearest verb before them in their sentence is a contact or communication verb, or they open their sentence and the next verb is one - and only the hours phrase is masked (maskGroup): 'CLSD DURING THE OFFICE HOURS OF THE CAA' is a review, 'CLSD. CONTACT CAA DURING NORMAL OFFICE HOURS' is not. Genuine non-time numbers are benign by what governs them: a label of the noun before it (TERMINAL 7, ALERT LVL 2, YUKON 1-5), a count of the noun after it (3 BOATS), a list or section label before a word, a letter-led designator (Q907, RWY13R, LEMOD-N644-DOBAT), a runway end, a location identifier, a visibility after VIS, a FICON code, a DME distance; each states holdsNoTemporal (it never holds a temporal token of the unmasked text), and a count or list label never follows a restriction verb directly. A class that states maskGroup masks only that group of its match. QA514 round 2 - four general syntactic rules, each a context that makes a number benign, none masking a clock-like shape, the object of a temporal connective (unless self-evident) or a range side: G1 an identifier starts with a letter - a token that starts with a letter and carries digits glued to it (directly, or by a hyphen, slash or dot: S0840, LT2168, TD132, TRAC2000/RSM970, EKCHHOJ0001035, LFAY.22.2, UTDD-145,146) is one identifier, never a clock, and a digit group glued by a hyphen to a letter never starts a clock-like shape; never letters that are a temporal word governing the digits (TO1000, H24, SR0600, AUG26), letters for digits (O800) or a time suffix closing the digits (Q800Z); a time designator (Z, L, LT, LCL, UTC, GMT, H, T) glued to a valid clock (HH 00-23, MM 00-59, or 2400: Z0800, LT0800, UTC0800-1000, H0800) is temporal content (designatedClock), never an identifier, while on an invalid clock (LT2168: minute 68) it is an identifier's letters; a four-digit group glued to letters is never masked after a temporal connective (UNTIL S0840 is a review). A digit-led identifier is one or two digits and letters that are never a time letter or word (Z, L, H, J, UTC, LT, HR ...), a letter for a digit, a unit or an ordinal (4D, 15D, 9D, (4A)), never after a duration's lead (FOR 8D). G2 a number governed by a measurement or designation noun - the head directly before it in its phrase (RWY 24, HGT FT AMSL: 422.24, L.R.147, D 3.9, NR RF 4/7) or directly after it (25 THR, 121.605 FREQUENCY, 20 TAC, 49 USC, 2.2 TO SSYEM, 473 FT; a unit glued after a number is its head, so 200M is a quantity, never a clock-like range side) is benign; after a temporal connective only a head after the number makes it self-evident (AT 25 THR, TO 121.605 FREQUENCY); a designation is a whole number. G3 structure: a list label opening a body line (atLineStart: '2. 60MIN PN', '3. EXPECT') or a clause ('(1)12MIN', '3.2.2 45.93 FT', vertex ordinals before positions), a statute's bracketed sub-paragraphs (40103(B)(3)) and an AIP page after a spaced hyphen (AD 2.24.11 - 5) are benign - never after a temporal connective, never a range side, never before a time word. G4 contact strings: a telephone number in spaced groups after its label or + country code, an e-mail address after AT (its @ written, (AT), or lost to a space). QA516: a digit is ANY Unicode decimal digit (accountedResidue category Nd): a digit of another script (Arabic-Indic, Devanagari ...) is never read as a value - left in the free text it is unaccounted for, a review - and a benign span never touches one (benignNeverTouches).

QA518 (governance is punctuation-invariant; a temporal qualification is accounted for whole). I5: every relation the rules read - a temporal connective and its object, a head noun and its number, a contact verb and its hours - is read on the SYNTACTIC text (syntax): each body line with every piece of punctuation that can only wrap or join tokens removed - quotes of every kind unless glued on both sides (O'CLOCK) or a unit mark after a digit (3000'), wrapping brackets, parentheses and braces (an opener glued to its token stays: OCA(OCH)), an ellipsis, a colon not between digits, a dash that joins no range - and spaces normalised; clauses end only at clauseBoundary (a semicolon, or a period followed by a space or the end; a period inside a number is never a boundary), defined once and read by contactHours and temporalObject alike. Every pattern is written for that text, so inserting or removing such punctuation anywhere around a span never changes a masking decision: 'UNTIL "121.35"', 'UNTIL [121.35]', 'UNTIL - 121.35' and 'UNTIL : 121.35' read as 'UNTIL 121.35' - a review; the field's lines and the free text's lines are each joined into one stream and read again, so punctuation across a line break reads as within a line. A connective's same-role synonyms are the same connective in every list (connectiveSynonyms: UNTIL/TILL/TIL, AFTER/AFT, BEFORE/BFR, DURING/DRG, BETWEEN/BTN, FROM/FM, EXCEPT/EXC). I1: numeric content in words is numeric content (accountedResidue.words: ZERO, ONE..NINETY and compounds, HUNDRED, HALF, QUARTER, NOON, MIDNIGHT, O'CLOCK); unmasked, it must lie in a statement the grammar reads, and the grammar reads no clock or time zone from words, so a word clock is a review ('AFTER HALF PAST EIGHT'); a number word is benign only by what governs it (a count of the noun after it, a label after its noun, the pronoun ONE, HALF OF a thing; numberWord). I6: in a sentence (found on the unmasked syntactic text) that holds a restriction - a restriction predicate (CLSD, U/S, AVBL, ACT, RESTRICTED ...; the noun OPS is operations, NO OPS a prohibition) - the object of every temporal connective (temporalObject.connectives: UNTIL, TILL, TIL, AFTER, BEFORE, SINCE, WEF; DURING, OUTSIDE; AT, FROM, BTN/BETWEEN and the end of a FROM range; EXCEPT, EXC, ONLY) is temporal content - a token that must lie in a statement the grammar reads and accounts for against Item D or B/C, else a review - whether or not it holds a digit or a known time word, unless it is POSITIVELY classified as not temporal: by a benign mask on its head, or by a role its connective admits (admits: a place for every connective; the notice's own stated content by anaphora for a period; traffic, works, authority, equipment, an action, a notice's lead time (AT SHORT NOTICE), a governing facility and codes in a structure of codes for a spatial connective; those and a predicate or a condition for an exception). An unclassified object is never 'no schedule'.

QA520 (an operand is accounted for whole). I8: every temporal connective creates an obligation, entered in one ledger per decision and checked once, at the end - no path reaches 'no schedule' while one is undischarged. In a sentence that holds a restriction it is discharged only when its operand is read and every unclassified token of it lies in a statement the grammar reads whole and proves against Item D or B/C, or when every content token of the operand is positively classified as not temporal (I7); in any other sentence the connective qualifies no restriction, but it must still have its operand. A missing operand discharges nothing: the connective at the end of its clause, line or record, a comma, period or semicolon right after it (unless a coordinated preposition or verb shares its operand: 'AT OR BLW 3000FT'), skip or function words only ('UNTIL THE.'), AND/OR or OF with nothing after it ('BTN TWY B AND.'): 'TWY J CLSD UNTIL.' and 'TWY Y CLSD AFTER, CURFEW.' are reviews. The operand is read whole - never cut at a word count; it ends at a boundary, a stop, restriction or noun-phrase-ending word, a verb, a label, a head-only noun or the end of the statement that holds it. I7: the operand is benign only if EVERY content token of it is positively classified as consistent with a role its connective admits (temporalObject.admits); one unclassified, temporal or event token makes it temporal content - a role word anywhere in it licenses nothing else. The head of a noun phrase is defined by composition (head-final: its last content token that is not a designator), so a place word never classifies a temporal, event or unknown head: 'DURING AIRPORT CURFEW', 'DURING CURFEW AT AIRPORT', 'AFTER RWY 08R CURFEW', 'DURING LOCAL CURFEW HOURS' are reviews, as 'DURING CURFEW' is. A modifier role classifies a word only before a designated head ('AFTER ACFT STAND 517L'); a temporal modifier only as the head of OF and a place or - when it is also a place word (boundPart: END) - bound to a designated place right after or right before it ('AT RWY 01R END', 'BTN APCH END RWY 25L AND TWY B'; 'AFTER RWY END' stays a review); a mask in a time-taking connective's operand only as the governance would mask it right after the connective, never over a canonical clock ('UNTIL AIRPORT 121.35', 'UNTIL RUNWAY 1000' are reviews); and every token after a pre-modifier is read again right after the connective, so a pre-modifier never hides temporal content ('DURING AIRPORT ACTIVATION' is 'DURING ACTIVATION'). Places the briefing itself names are places by role (temporalObject.gazetteer): the decision is handed, as data built once per analysis from the OFP's own lines, the words of every NOTAM bulletin station heading's name and FIR heading's name, their location indicators and every five-letter fix a route string names next to DCT or an airway - 'AT VELANA INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (VRMM)' is a place in a briefing whose bulletin heads 'VRMM /MLE MALE/VELANA INTL', a review in any other; a gazetteer word never classifies a temporal token, a temporal modifier or a time word, and never a head it does not name ('DURING VELANA CURFEW' is a review). A degree word (degree: IMMEDIATELY, DIRECTLY ...) is part of a place only directly before a place direction (direction: 'A POINT IMMEDIATELY SOUTH OF TWY D2'). A numeric list label that opens no body line is, after AND/OR, the next conjunct's number, not a new item ('BTN SSYEF AND 2.2 TO SSYEM').

QA520 continuation: a full structured study reference is metadata only when attached to an already wholly classified spatial place. It cannot supply a missing place or license a temporal operand. A comma and coordinator followed by a subject and finite predicate begins an independent clause, not another noun in the preceding object. No clause content is masked: all of its timing tokens and connectives remain accountable.

Grammar, after upper-casing, folding dashes, DAILY->DLY, dropping EVERY/EV/AND, dropping UTC/Z after a time and closing spaces around '-': date parts and time ranges alternate; a date token after a time closes an entry; ',' ';' ':' only separate. A date part is DLY, weekdays (MON-FRI ranges allowed), month days (AUG 12 14 15, AUG 01-05), or a cross-month range (JUL 20-SEP 30). Day numbers with no month take the latest month named earlier in the field, else the validity month when B and C are in one month, else a timing review. Every day must exist: a day past its month's length, or 29 FEB when no leap year falls within the validity, is a timing review. An entry with no date part is daily only when it is the first entry. Times are HHMM-HHMM with HH 00-23 and MM 00-59 (an end before the start crosses midnight; an end equal to the start, such as 1800-1800, is a timing review: no LIDO or ICAO convention for a zero-length range is held here, so it is neither read as 24 hours nor as nothing) or H24. Anything else is a timing review.
Occurrences are clipped to the validity.

Validity not overlapping the window: outside_window (outsideBy validity), decided before any source or schedule review - schedule text that cannot be read cannot put a notice in force outside its own validity; the state is the validity's relation to the reference.

review: the validity could not be read (absent or unreadable start or end), or it overlaps the window and the source record or the schedule could not be read; state unknown_at_reference, no minutes, no reference interval.

With a schedule: occurrences overlapping the window make it affecting; the state is the occurrence covering the reference, else the next one after it, else the last one before it. With none in the window: outside_window, and the state is read from every occurrence searched (validity, at most lookbackDays before the window, and openEndSearchDays after it for an open end).
Without a schedule: affecting; the state is the validity's relation to the reference.
No reference instant: state unknown_at_reference with the status above.
minutesDelta: 0 when active, minutes to the start when it begins after, minutes since the end when it ended before.

reviewReasons.validity: The LIDO VALID range could not be read; the timing is unresolved.
reviewReasons.reviewLanguage: Schedule uses daylight, exception, or holiday rules that are not evaluated; the timing is unresolved.
reviewReasons.freeText: The LIDO record contains schedule language inside free text; the timing is unresolved.
reviewReasons.freeTextConflict: The LIDO record states schedule hours in its free text that its Item D does not account for; the timing is unresolved.

rules: A notice printing dated runway-closure regimes (WSSS SX120/25) is decided per runway: each regime with an occurrence on the reference day, or the previous evening's occurrence still running at the reference, yields that runway's state; the notice itself stays a timing review when other schedule language remains.
